tagline: "Or what to do when some dependencies are optional"

#### ! Scenario

*Or what to do when some dependencies are optional*
Python merges two JVM ideas into one scenario. **Extras** are optional *runtime* features a package offers (`demo-lib-a[feature]`) — the sibling of Maven optional dependencies ([MS8](../../maven-demo/scenario-8-optional/guide.qmd)). **Dependency groups** are optional *development* sets (test, docs, lint) — the sibling of build scopes ([MS7](../../maven-demo/scenario-7-scopes/guide.qmd)). This scenario shows both.

::: {.callout-note title="Tool Versions"}
Tested with **pip 25.3**, **Poetry 2.4**, **uv 0.11**. Extras are standard (PEP 508) everywhere. Dependency groups converged late. Poetry groups arrived in 1.2 with their own `[tool.poetry.group.*]` syntax; the standard `[dependency-groups]` table (PEP 735) is read by uv (0.4.27+), by Poetry (2.2+) and — since 25.1 — by `pip install --group`. All three legs of this demo use that one table. Before 25.1, pip's only idiom was multiple requirements files, and it remains the common one in the wild.
:::

#### ! Example

Extras — opting in pulls the optional `demo-lib-d`:

```{.text include="pip/requirements-extras.txt" snippet="p7-extras"}
```

Groups — a dev-only set, installed or skipped on demand. This is the standard PEP 735 table; uv, Poetry 2.2+ and `pip install --group` (25.1+) all read it:

```{.toml include="uv/pyproject.toml" snippet="p7-uv-group"}
```

#### ! Expect
Optional dependencies come along by default.

#### ! Actual
Half right. Plain `demo-lib-a` does **not** install `demo-lib-d`; `demo-lib-a[feature]` does — extras are opt-in everywhere. The `dev` *group* is a different story, because each tool's default differs:

*   **pip** — absent unless requested; `pip install --group dev` (25.1+) includes it.
*   **Poetry** — **present by default**: every non-optional group installs with `poetry install`; `--without dev` leaves it out, and `optional = true` on the group makes it opt-in.
*   **uv** — present by default (`dev` is uv's default group); `--no-dev` excludes it.

The older pip idiom — `requirements.txt` plus `requirements-dev.txt` as separate files — still dominates in the wild.

#### ! Why
Extras and groups both answer "don't make everyone pay for what only some need", but at different layers. An extra is published *by the library* as a named bundle of optional runtime deps — consumers opt in with `[name]`. A group is defined *by your project* for its own workflow (tests, docs) and never ships to consumers. The JVM splits these across `<optional>true</optional>` and build scopes; Python's extras + groups cover the same ground with different seams.

#### ! Fix
*   **Offering optional features in a library:** declare an extra, so consumers write `your-lib[feature]`.
*   **Separating dev tooling:** use the standard `[dependency-groups]` table, which pip 25.1+, Poetry 2.2+ and uv all read; on older pip, a second requirements file.
*   **Installing:** `pip install "pkg[extra]"`; `pip install --group dev` (25.1+); `poetry install` (groups included) or `--without dev`; `uv sync` (groups included) or `--no-dev` — check what your default install actually pulls, because the defaults disagree.

#### ! Risk
* LOW Declaring a clean extra for a genuinely optional feature.
* MEDIUM Putting test/lint tools in main dependencies instead of a group — every consumer and every production image now carries pytest.
* HIGH Relying on an extra being installed when your deploy step omits it; the feature imports fine locally and `ImportError`s in production.

#### ! Check

**Fast check:**

```bash
pip install -r requirements.txt        && ! pip show demo-lib-d   # absent
pip install -r requirements-extras.txt &&   pip show demo-lib-d   # present
pip install --group dev       # demo-lib-d present (pip 25.1+, reads pyproject.toml)
poetry install                # demo-lib-d present — groups install by default
poetry install --without dev  # no demo-lib-d
uv sync                       # demo-lib-d present — dev is uv's default group
uv sync --no-dev              # no demo-lib-d
```

**What to look for:** `demo-lib-d` present only when the extra is requested; for the group, present by default under Poetry and uv, absent by default under pip.

**Conclusion:** Extras are opt-in everywhere; groups are opt-in on pip and opt-out on Poetry and uv.

#### ! Takeaway
Python folds the JVM's optional dependencies and build scopes into extras (runtime, published by the library) and dependency groups (dev, defined by your project). Groups only became a cross-tool standard recently — PEP 735, read by uv, Poetry 2.2+ and pip 25.1+ — and the tools still disagree on whether a group installs by default. Mind both gaps.

#### ! Wild
The classic extras example is `pip install "requests[security]"` — for years that pulled cryptography-backed TLS extras that plain `requests` left out. It was also a classic footgun: countless bug reports of "requests can't do X" turned out to be "you installed requests, not requests[the-extra-you-needed]".
